name: Temple of Seti I (Abydos)
scope: The surviving Temple of Seti I at Abydos, with its twelve-pier entrance portico, roofed double hypostyle halls and side wing, seven chapel bays and the immediate ruined forecourts.
era: The standing archaeological site, with the exterior photographed in 1990

references.artist: The original uploader was Chapultepec at English Wikipedia.

originalReview.notes: The exact public-domain Qualla photograph records the surviving flat-roof portico and ruined court in 1990. ARCE and Bell document the twelve square piers, central main door, limestone walls and relative organization of both hypostyle halls.

review.method: Exact local Qualla public-domain original, independent native mapping and early architectural documentation.
review.notes: Inspected the exact Qualla exterior original first. It matches the photographer Chapultepec’s self-made photo and native public-domain dedication. Bell’s expired 1915 survey supplies the historical plan and section.
